findings.evidence: SOURCE 1 identifies the current protocol as 'WeirdML (v3)' and lists 'Previous versions: WeirdML v2 · WeirdML v1'. The row claims version '2' and guard 'Verify the published version 2 before reading results.', which contradicts the current published version.
findings.repair: Update the row to version 3 and refresh identity/metric/description accordingly, or mark this row retained/superseded while preserving version 2; do not present version 2 as the current protocol.

findings.evidence: Row metric says 'Average Max Accuracy ... 5 iterations ... averaged over all 17 tasks'. SOURCE 1 v3 scoring is '80% normalized area under its line on a logarithmic token axis, plus 20% of its final value' over 11 tasks, with no max-accuracy convention.
findings.repair: Set scoring.metric to the v3 official score definition (11 tasks, normalized-area + final-value), or supply the v2 protocol excerpt if the row is intentionally for version 2.

findings.evidence: SOURCE 1 names WeirdML v3 as the current version and lists v2 as a previous version, thereby naming v3 as the successor; the row's superseded_by is null.
findings.repair: Populate superseded_by with the registry id of the successor board (v3), or provide evidence that no successor exists.

findings.evidence: SOURCE 1 describes v3 as 11 agentic tasks to explore unfamiliar data and build ML/data-analysis pipelines under limited data, unspecified goals and limited feedback. The row describes PyTorch code under fixed compute and time limits, terms not present in the protocol excerpt.
findings.repair: Align description with the v3 protocol text or provide v2 evidence if retaining version 2.

uncertainties: Accepted SOURCE 2 nonzero change count as affirmative evidence for status 'active'; I did not fail status even though the page lists v2 as previous, because the protocol does not explicitly retire v2 and activity supports active.
The successor registry id for v3 is not supplied in the packet; the superseded_by repair depends on our registry and cannot be verified from this evidence alone.
Hash and transport checks are owner responsibilities and were not executable here; I did not independently verify the supplied sha256 values.
The description discrepancy may stem from intended v2 versus current v3; no v2 protocol excerpt is present to resolve that ambiguity.
